Restore turbo cache:
if: ${{ steps.lane-verdict.outputs.hit != 'true' }}
        uses: actions/cache/restore@v4
        with:
          path: .turbo
          key: turbo-build-${{ github.sha }}
          restore-keys: |
            turbo-build-
Build:
if: ${{ steps.lane-verdict.outputs.hit != 'true' }}
        shell: bash
        env:
          SELECTION_BASE: ${{ steps.selection.outputs.base-sha }}
        # PR: --affected builds only the touched packages (plus dependents via
        # turbo's graph; upstream deps still build as prerequisites). Push:
        # everything.
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          if [ "$GITHUB_EVENT_NAME" = "pull_request" ] && [ -n "$SELECTION_BASE" ]; then
            pnpm turbo run build --affected 2>&1 | tee build.log
          else
            pnpm turbo run build 2>&1 | tee build.log
          fi
Save turbo cache:
if: ${{ (github.event_name != 'pull_request') && steps.lane-verdict.outputs.hit != 'true' }}
        uses: actions/cache/save@v4
        with:
          path: .turbo
          key: turbo-build-${{ github.sha }}

  # Sizes the integration matrix before any expensive setup. It is its own job
  # because `strategy.matrix` cannot be built from an input expression — a
  # matrix reads a JSON array, and a job output is the only place a reusable
  # workflow can produce one. It installs nothing, so the cost is a runner
  # start; the matrix it sizes is what waits.
